title: Cut the tax burden on labour: a cap on social contributions (the 'development cap') and then a higher general income-tax allowance
description: The 2026–2030 coalition agreement of the SDS, NSi, SLS, Fokus and the Democrats promises relief for labour, changes to the income-tax scale, higher net wages and a predictable tax environment without new burdens (Siol summary). Its main vehicle is the Act on Interventions for the Development of Slovenia (the 'development act'), which caps social-security contributions on higher salaries; Janša presents a higher general income-tax allowance as the next step once the act is in force.
reasoning: The National Assembly passed the development act, which NSi, SLS, Fokus, the Democrats and Resni.ca had tabled before the government took office, with SDS votes. The trade unions sought a subsequent legislative referendum; parliament declared it inadmissible, the Constitutional Court annulled that decision, and the act is suspended until the vote on 6 December 2026. On 19 October 2026 Janša told parliament that raising the general allowance would follow the act's entry into force and that the Strategic Council for the Economy was finalising further tax proposals, so the commitment is under way but not delivered.
key_evidence: Coalition agreement signed on 21 May 2026: relief for labour, changes to the income-tax scale, higher net wages (Siol)

Development act tabled by NSi, SLS, Fokus, the Democrats and Resni.ca and passed with SDS votes; Constitutional Court annulled parliament's decision that the unions' referendum was inadmissible (24ur, 11 September 2026)
Subsequent legislative referendum on the act on 6 December 2026 (24ur, 19 October 2026)
19 October 2026: Janša called a higher general income-tax allowance 'one of the next key steps' after the act enters into force (gov.si)

title: Set up SKOK, a specialised prosecution body and court for corruption and organised crime
description: The coalition agreement lists the fight against corruption and organised crime among its four core priorities and devotes two articles to creating SKOK, a unit for prosecuting corruption and organised crime. At the signing, Democrats leader Anže Logar spoke of 'serious political will' to create 'a strong prosecutorial body' with police and judicial pillars.
reasoning: The National Assembly passed the SKOK act under the urgent procedure on 24 September 2026 by 47 votes to 35, and it entered into force in October 2026. It turns the Specialised State Prosecutor's Office into a dedicated prosecution body and creates a Specialised Court, but both start work only on 1 July 2027, so the legislative part is done and the bodies themselves are not yet operating. The judiciary and prosecution criticised the act as insufficiently thought through, and the opposition warned of political subordination of prosecution.
key_evidence: Coalition agreement of 21 May 2026: two articles on creating SKOK (Primorske novice)
24 September 2026: SKOK act passed 47–35 under the urgent procedure (RTV SLO)
Act in force since October 2026; the renamed prosecution office and the Specialised Court start work on 1 July 2027 (RTV SLO, 17 October 2026)

title: End the previous government's measures against Israel and reset relations
description: Janša, a critic of the Golob government's 2024 recognition of a Palestinian state and of its measures against Israel, wrote on taking office that 'the time has come for a responsible Slovenian foreign policy based on facts, Slovenian national interests and international law' and that the 'politically and economically harmful period of government support for activist anti-Semitism' had ended (JTA).
reasoning: On the day he was elected the Palestinian flag was removed from a government building; the government then revoked the measures its predecessor had adopted against Israel and, at the end of August 2026, prevented the adoption of an EU joint statement condemning the conduct of Israeli settlers in the West Bank. Israel opened its first resident embassy in Ljubljana, accompanied by a visit of Foreign Minister Gideon Saar. The reversal was carried out as announced; the Freedom Movement and the Left responded with a motion for a constitutional indictment of the Prime Minister.
key_evidence: 22 May 2026: Palestinian flag lowered from a government building less than an hour after Janša's election (JTA)
Government revoked the predecessor's measures against Israel; Slovenia blocked an EU statement on West Bank settlers at the end of August (24ur, 11 September 2026)

Israel opened a resident embassy in Ljubljana, with a visit by Foreign Minister Gideon Saar (24ur, 11 September 2026); Freedom Movement and the Left filed a constitutional-indictment motion on 9 September 2026 (RTV SLO)

title: Modernise the armed forces and meet Slovenia's NATO defence-spending commitment
description: The coalition agreement pledges to modernise the Slovenian Armed Forces, improve their staffing and readiness, and stresses an active role in the EU and NATO (Siol summary). The government presented its first budget revision as bringing defence spending to 2.03% of GDP and so fulfilling Slovenia's commitment to NATO.
reasoning: The supplementary 2026 budget, adopted by the National Assembly on 1 October 2026, adds €296 million for defence and takes the defence ministry's budget above €1.7 billion, which the government says equals 2.03% of GDP; the main purchases include the IRIS-T SLM air-defence system, whose batteries are due between 2027 and 2029, and Caesar artillery. The target is budgeted rather than spent and the modernisation is multi-year, so the commitment is advancing but not completed. The Fiscal Council warned that the revision departs further from Slovenia's medium-term fiscal commitments.
key_evidence: Coalition agreement: modernise the armed forces, active role in NATO (Siol)
Budget revision adds €296 million for defence, 2.03% of GDP according to the government (24ur, 11 September 2026)
Defence ministry budget above €1.7 billion; IRIS-T SLM orders worth €371.8 million, batteries due from 2027 to 2029 (RTV SLO, 16 September 2026)
1 October 2026: National Assembly adopted the revision; Janša said defence spending was above 2% of GDP for the first time since 1992 (RTV SLO)

title: Restrict the right to vote in local elections to Slovenian and EU citizens
description: The coalition amended the Local Elections Act to remove the right of third-country nationals to vote in municipal elections, and also asked voters in a consultative referendum whether local voting rights should belong only to Slovenian and EU citizens.
reasoning: The amendment was adopted and took effect after opponents withdrew their referendum initiative before collecting signatures; it applies to the local elections of November 2026, although the opposition has asked the Constitutional Court to review it. In the consultative referendum of 11 October 2026, 55.30% of voters backed the restriction. A pending constitutional review could still change the outcome.
key_evidence: Local Elections Act amended; in force for the November 2026 local elections; opposition referred it to the Constitutional Court (24ur, 11 September 2026)
Consultative referendum called by the National Assembly on 28 August 2026 (State Election Commission)
11 October 2026: 55.30% for, 44.70% against (RTV SLO, from State Election Commission data)

title: Abolish the compulsory RTV Slovenija licence fee
description: With Resni.ca, the coalition called a consultative referendum on abolishing the compulsory contribution that funds the public broadcaster RTV Slovenija, and it urged a 'yes' vote on all four referendum questions of 11 October 2026. A bill by Resni.ca leader Zoran Stevanović to abolish the fee and fund RTV from the state budget had been pending in the National Assembly since November 2025.
reasoning: Voters narrowly rejected abolition in the consultative referendum (49.97% for, 50.03% against, a margin of 546 votes), so the fee remains. In August 2026 Stevanović, by then Speaker of the National Assembly, proposed deferring the committee reading of the Resni.ca bill until after the referendum, and the Assembly's legislative service called its key provisions constitutionally contentious. On 19 October 2026 Janša said the result showed divided opinion and that consultative referendums guide rather than bind the legislature; no step to abolish the fee had been taken as of October 2026.
key_evidence: 28 August 2026: National Assembly called the consultative referendum (State Election Commission)
Coalition and Resni.ca urged '4x ZA' (sl.wikipedia, citing the parties)
August 2026: legislative service called the Resni.ca bill's key provisions constitutionally contentious; Stevanović proposed deferring its committee reading until after the referendum (RTV SLO)
11 October 2026: 49.97% for, 50.03% against (RTV SLO)
19 October 2026: Janša said opinion on the fee was divided (24ur, gov.si)

title: Make cash social assistance for people able to work conditional on community work
description: The coalition asked voters in a consultative referendum whether the right to cash social assistance (denarna socialna pomoč) for people able to work and without objective obstacles to work should depend on their active performance of community work.
reasoning: Voters approved the principle with 60.54% in the consultative referendum of 11 October 2026. A consultative referendum does not change the law by itself, and no amendment to the social-assistance legislation was reported as tabled or adopted in the sources reviewed for this profile as of October 2026, so the commitment has advanced only to the stage of a popular mandate.
key_evidence: 28 August 2026: consultative referendum called (State Election Commission)
11 October 2026: 60.54% for, 39.46% against (RTV SLO)

title: Fix the long-term care system: equal payments for care-home residents and a €300 supplement for care workers
description: The government drafted a law on temporary measures for a more effective long-term care system, equalising what care-home residents pay whether or not they already have a long-term care decision and introducing a temporary supplement of €300 gross a month for long-term care and home-help workers.
reasoning: The National Assembly adopted the act on 18 September 2026 by 61 votes to none, and it took effect on 1 October 2026: all care-home residents now pay the same for the same services, those disadvantaged since 1 December 2025 can receive a credit, and full-time care and home-help workers receive the €300 supplement. The measures are temporary, as the act's title says.
key_evidence: Bill prepared by the government with equal payments and a €300 gross supplement (24ur, 11 September 2026)
18 September 2026: adopted 61–0 (RTV SLO)
1 October 2026: measures in force (RTV SLO)

title: Hold down fuel and energy prices, including a temporary cut in energy taxes
description: Janša has made energy prices a priority, saying that 'all available options at both European and national levels' should be used to stabilise them. The development act includes the option of cutting taxes on energy products for nine months, which he says could lower prices by about 10%.
reasoning: Soon after taking office the government extended the regulation of fuel prices for six months while raising traders' maximum margins, asked the European Commission to allow excise duties on motor fuels and heating oil below the EU minimum, and prepared an amendment to the Excise Duties Act and a law protecting food and transport supply from fuel costs. The nine-month energy-tax cut in the development act is blocked until the referendum of 6 December 2026, so the measures are partial and ongoing.
key_evidence: Fuel-price regulation extended for six months; maximum margins raised (24ur, 11 September 2026)
Request to Brussels to cut excise duties below the EU minimum; draft amendment to the Excise Duties Act (24ur)
19 October 2026: Janša said the nine-month energy-tax cut was delayed by the referendum process (gov.si)

title: A 'cheaper state but with better quality': a smaller government, leaner public administration and less red tape
description: Before his election Janša told reporters that the coalition would ensure 'a cheaper state but with better quality' (Al Jazeera). The coalition agreement announces rationalisation of public administration, digitalisation and the use of artificial intelligence in state services, simpler procedures and decentralisation.
reasoning: The government took office with 15 ministers, five fewer than the Golob government, and ministries were reorganised. Janša has announced a restructuring of the public sector in response to criticism of the growth in the number of public employees, but no such reform had been adopted as of October 2026, and the budget revision raised spending by 6.2%.
key_evidence: Janša: the coalition will ensure 'a cheaper state but with better quality' (Al Jazeera, May 2026)
Coalition agreement: rationalisation and digitalisation of public administration (Siol)
15 ministers, five fewer than in the previous government; ministries reorganised; public-sector restructuring announced (24ur, 11 September 2026)

title: No measure that endangers fiscal sustainability
description: The coalition agreement provides that any measure increasing spending or reducing revenue of the state, municipal or other public budgets must be designed so that it does not jeopardise fiscal sustainability; on 15 June 2026 Janša and Finance Minister Andrej Šircelj told the Fiscal Council that 'the Government will honour this commitment'.
reasoning: The budget revision adopted on 1 October 2026 plans a deficit of €2.2 billion, or 2.9% of GDP, which the finance minister says complies with the fiscal rules. The Fiscal Council said it departs further from Slovenia's medium-term commitments, that net expenditure growth again exceeds the permitted level and that it contains no measures for a lasting improvement, expecting corrective measures in the 2027–2028 budgets. With the official assessments in conflict and those budgets still pending, the verdict is provisional.
key_evidence: 15 June 2026: government pledges to honour the coalition agreement's fiscal-sustainability clause (gov.si)
Budget revision: deficit €2.2 billion, 2.9% of GDP, 'in line with the fiscal rules' according to the finance minister (gov.si, 11 September 2026)
Fiscal Council: revision is a further departure from the medium-term plan (RTV SLO, 28 September 2026)

title: Reform the school system and establish an 'ideologically neutral school'
description: Janša told the National Assembly that the coalition agreement commits the government to 'the establishment of an ideologically neutral school guaranteed by Article 41 of the Constitution', with the goals of removing ideological content from kindergartens and schools, raising the status of the teaching profession and restoring teachers' authority. Education Minister Borut Rončević has announced a comprehensive reform, including replacing the nine-year primary school with an eight-year one.
reasoning: After the PISA 2025 results the ministry announced the reform, and an expert council for it has been formed; no reform legislation was reported as adopted by October 2026. Representatives of the education system urged a careful approach, and opposition deputies criticised the council's composition, which Janša defended on 19 October 2026. Concrete preparatory steps exist, so the verdict is in progress.
key_evidence: Minister Rončević announced a comprehensive reform, including abolishing the nine-year primary school (24ur, 11 September 2026)
19 October 2026: Janša cited the coalition agreement's 'ideologically neutral school' and defended the reform council (24ur, gov.si)
